You are part of a thorough, READ-ONLY audit of Nxeon, a LIVE VPS/game-server/web-hosting business. Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router + server actions + Prisma + Postgres). Read /opt/nxeon/CLAUDE.md first. Customer portal is app/dashboard/** (Shell: components/nx/Shell.tsx). Server actions live mostly in lib/actions*.ts; background work runs in worker/*.ts via `Job` rows (dispatch table at worker/index.ts ~line 2215; every JobType enum value has a handler there).

STRICT RULES (live production): READ-ONLY. Do not edit/create/delete any file under /opt. Do not run npm/npx/tsc/prisma/build, any scripts/*, systemctl, pkill, or anything that mutates state. DB: SELECT-only via `sudo -u postgres psql -d nxeon -c "..."`, never write. Never print secrets, password hashes, tokens, or customer emails/PII (aggregate counts only). Do not touch the live site.

YOUR SCOPE: the customer VPS server section (NOT game servers — skip the game branch of app/dashboard/servers/[id] and anything game-only):
- app/dashboard/servers/page.tsx and app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx (1516 lines — read the VPS branch fully) and every component it renders for VPS tabs.
- For each VPS feature: power (start/stop/reboot), reinstall (OS choice), resize (up/down, proration), snapshots (create/delete/rollback), backups (create/restore/schedule/download?), firewall, port forwards, SSH keys, reverse DNS (rDNS), console (VNC/serial/web terminal), metrics/usage graphs, networking (IPs, dedicated IP add-on, private networking), password reset, disk expand, cancel/delete, auto-renew toggle on the server, rescue mode / ISO mount if any.
- app/dashboard/volumes (block storage) and app/dashboard/nxcloud.
For every feature, follow the chain UI component -> server action (lib/actions-server*.ts, actions-firewall.ts, actions-backup.ts, actions-volumes.ts, actions-dedicated-ip.ts, actions-disk.ts, actions-nxcloud.ts, etc.) -> job enqueue -> worker handler (worker/index.ts, worker/volumes.ts, worker/firewall.ts, worker/network.ts, worker/restore.ts, worker/nxcloud.ts ...) and determine whether it genuinely works end-to-end. READ THE ACTUAL CODE, not just filenames.

Look specifically for: TODO/FIXME/"not implemented"/"coming soon"/stub handlers; server actions that return success without doing anything; errors caught and swallowed silently (empty catch, catch returning ok) where that hides a real failure from the customer; UI buttons with no handler or hrefs to non-existent routes (verify each href target exists under /opt/nxeon/app/); features gated behind env flags (check /opt/nxeon/.env for flag NAMES only — `grep -o '^[A-Z_]*=' /opt/nxeon/.env` style, never print values); missing ownership checks (does each action verify server.userId === current user?); money paths that charge without delivering or deliver without charging; worker handlers that mark DONE while doing nothing (e.g. SANDBOX branches); UI copy that promises something the code doesn't do; rDNS that just stores a string but never applies it; metrics that silently show empty.
Also check the DB (SELECT only) for signs of breakage: e.g. `SELECT type, status, count(*) FROM "Job" WHERE "createdAt" > now() - interval '30 days' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2;` and look at failure clusters for VPS job types (you may SELECT the error text of failed jobs, truncating to 200 chars and redacting anything that looks like a secret/IP-password). Check the actual table/column names via `\d "Job"` first.

DELIVERABLE (final message, no files): a prioritized findings list. Each item: severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low), feature, what's wrong/missing, evidence (file path:line or SQL result), why it matters to a paying customer, one-line suggested fix direction. Then a short list of VPS features that are confirmed working end-to-end (one line each, with the handler reference) so the coordinator knows what's solid. Then a list of what's conspicuously missing vs DigitalOcean/Hetzner Cloud/Vultr (e.g. rescue mode, ISO mount, floating IPs, private networking, firewall groups, monitoring alerts, scheduled backups with restore, bandwidth accounting, resize-down, serial console) — state for each whether it's absent, half-built, or present, with evidence. Be specific; don't pad.

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).

- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

content.text:
# Nxeon VPS audit: prioritized findings

I traced each VPS feature from the button through the server action and job to the worker handler. Two of the problems below need fixing first:
- **Critical:** customer VMs behind the shared NAT address can reach each other freely.
- **High:** customer firewall rules are wiped on every reboot and never put back, while the panel still shows them as active.

---

## Findings (most severe first)

### Critical

**1. Networking / tenant isolation: all NAT customer VMs sit on one open private network.**
- **Evidence:**
  - `/etc/network/interfaces`: vmbr1 is a plain Linux bridge.
  - `bridge -d link show`: all 10 vmbr1 ports report `isolated off`.
  - `/proc/sys/net/bridge/bridge-nf-call-iptables` is `0`, so the host firewall never sees VM-to-VM traffic.
  - ebtables FORWARD is empty with policy ACCEPT.
  - `/etc/pve/firewall/` is empty, and no VM config has `firewall=1`.
  - The `nxeon_fw` nft table only filters traffic from vmbr1 to the host and out to the internet, not between VMs.
  - Staging VMs (.50–.99) share this same bridge with production.
- **Why it matters:** any tenant can reach every other tenant's private 10.20.0.x address on any port. That includes databases or admin panels a customer assumed were private. A tenant can also claim another tenant's IP (ARP spoofing) and hijack the inbound SSH/web traffic that NAT forwards to that address. The panel's wording, "private address … only routable inside our network" (`VpsNetworkingPanel.tsx`), makes this look safe when it isn't.
- **Fix:** turn on bridge port isolation for tap ports (or ebtables/PVE firewall with `firewall=1` plus IP filter / anti-spoof per NIC), and move staging to its own bridge. Confirm with two staging VMs first.

### High

**2. Firewall: rules vanish on reboot and are never re-applied, but the panel still lists them as active.**
- **Evidence:**
  - `buildReconcileScript` (`lib/firewall-rules.ts:230-253`) only runs iptables commands inside the guest; nothing saves them to survive a reboot.
  - The only thing that creates `SYNC_FIREWALL` jobs is a rule change in `lib/actions-firewall.ts`. Start, reboot, reinstall, resize, restore, rollback, dedicated-IP power cycles and the crash-recovery sweep never re-sync.
  - `syncFirewall` treats a STOPPED server as "defer", and the job is marked DONE (`worker/firewall.ts`).
  - DB: the only server with rules (8 enabled) last synced at 2026-09-02 15:03:08. It was rebooted at 15:03:53 and hasn't synced since.
  - A failed sync sends the customer no notification.
- **Why it matters:** the UI says rules "take effect within a minute", but the customer's actual protection is most likely gone. This is worst for dedicated-IP servers, where every port faces the internet directly.
- **Fix:** persist the rules in the guest (systemd unit or netfilter-persistent), enqueue `SYNC_FIREWALL` after every power and lifecycle job, show when rules were last applied, and notify on failure. Longer term, enforce at the hypervisor instead.

**3. Error state: any failed power or lifecycle job locks the customer out of the whole server page.**
- **Evidence:**
  - Failures of START, STOP, REBOOT, RESIZE, BACKUP_RESTORE, SNAPSHOT_ROLLBACK and ASSIGN_DEDICATED_IP set the server to ERROR (`worker/index.ts:106-112`, `2520-2522`).
  - The page then returns only the provisioning screen whenever status is ERROR (`page.tsx:340`, `376`). That screen shows "Provisioning failed" and a Contact support button (`components/nx/Provisioning.tsx:175-190`).
  - The retry banner (`ProvisionErrorBanner` / `retryProvision`, `page.tsx:1441`) is dead code for every server type, because the page returns before reaching it.
  - No sweep ever brings a server out of ERROR.
- **Why it matters:** one flaky reboot on an established, working VM takes away Start, the console, restore, cancel and refund. The message tells the customer "the server could not be built", which is wrong for a server that already exists.
- **Fix:** only show the full-page screen for first-time provisioning. For other failures, render the normal panel with an error banner, a Start/retry option, and the real job error.

**4. Billing: VPS customers can't renew manually or turn auto-renew back on (regression since 2026-09-12).**
- **Evidence:**
  - `renewalPanel` (the `RenewalCard` with Renew now and the auto-renew toggle) is defined at `page.tsx:455-482` but never rendered. Commit `013bb73dac` swapped it for the display-only `VpsSubscriptionCard`.
  - `toggleAutoRenew` and `renewNow` have no other caller anywhere in the customer portal.
- **Why it matters:** two messages promise controls that don't exist:
  - The cancel flow says "You can turn auto-renew back on any time before then" (`lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:396`).
  - The billing sweep tells customers "Renew manually before X" and links to the server page (`worker/billing.ts:335`).

  A customer who turns auto-renew off can't undo it, so the server expires, gets suspended and is eventually destroyed. No paid VPS has auto-renew off today. Two game servers do (expiring 2026-10-20), and the game branch doesn't render the card either.
- **Fix:** render `RenewalCard` again (for example in Settings or the subscription card).

**5. Worker: one serial job queue for the whole platform.**
- **Evidence:**
  - The worker claims one job at a time and awaits it inline (`worker/index.ts:3181-3200`). All the periodic sweeps (billing, VM crash recovery, uptime) run in that same loop.
  - A game install can wait up to 45 minutes per attempt (`provision-health.ts:257`), and a backup up to 1 hour (`index.ts:2170`).
  - Live right now: a game PROVISION has been RUNNING since 03:17 with 6 jobs queued behind it.
- **Why it matters:** a VPS customer's Reboot/Start/password reset, and the automatic restart of a crashed VM, wait behind other customers' long jobs. The "within a minute" firewall promise can't be met.
- **Fix:** add a separate fast lane for short VPS jobs (or run per-server jobs concurrently), and move the sweeps onto their own timer.

### Medium

**6. Snapshots: rollback can fail and then lock the server; no limits; failures are silent.**
- **Evidence:**
  - Storage `vmdata` is a ZFS pool (`/etc/pve/storage.cfg`). Proxmox's ZFS backend refuses to roll back to any snapshot that isn't the newest, yet the UI offers Rollback on every row.
  - A failed rollback sets the server to ERROR, which triggers the lockout in finding 3.
  - `createSnapshot` (`lib/actions-server.ts:62`) has no snapshot count or size limit, while the `data` pool is already 80% full and 70% fragmented (`zpool list`).
  - The app accepts names starting with a digit; Proxmox, as far as I know, requires a leading letter.
  - `snapshotOp` (`index.ts:1969-2033`) never notifies the customer on success or failure.
- **Fix:** only offer rollback on the newest snapshot, remove SNAPSHOT_ROLLBACK from the list of failures that set ERROR, cap snapshots per server, validate names the way Proxmox does, and notify on failure. Confirm the ZFS rollback behaviour on staging.

**7. Delete: the More → Delete path skips the refund.**
- `VpsPowerControls.tsx:124-137` calls `serverAction("delete")` (`lib/actions.ts:810-815`), which issues a plain DELETE with no refund. `cancelService` (`lifecycle.ts:405-471`) is the only path that refunds unused time.
- The dialog only says "Any remaining term is handled by the cancellation flow…" (line 133). The same path also destroys attached volumes without warning in the dialog.
- **Fix:** route Delete through `cancelService("immediate")`, or remove it from the menu.

**8. Power: Stop pulls the plug, and a hung guest can't be recovered cleanly.**
- STOP maps to Proxmox `status/stop` (`index.ts:1404`), which is an immediate power-off. There is no graceful shutdown and no reset.
- On a hung guest, Reboot (which needs the guest to cooperate) fails, and that feeds finding 3.
- **Fix:** add Shutdown (graceful) and Reset (hard) as separate actions, and make Stop graceful with a hard-stop fallback.

**9. Dedicated IPv4: advertised as included, but new servers silently get NAT when the pool runs out.**
- `provision()` only logs "This customer paid for an IP they did not receive" to the console and carries on with NAT (`index.ts:779-793`).
- Marketing claims a dedicated IPv4 comes with the VPS (`app/llms.txt/route.ts:73`, `app/(marketing)/gaming-vps/page.tsx:10`).
- DB: 11 of 17 VPS are on NAT, and the pool has 1 free customer IP left.
- **Fix:** alert an admin and tell the customer when this happens, or fix the marketing copy.

**10. Volumes: the advice for keeping volume data is impossible to follow.**
- Reinstall and restore refuse while a volume is assigned. The reinstall error tells the customer to "attach the volume to a different server first" (`lifecycle.ts:162-168`).
- `attachVolume` refuses exactly that (`actions-volumes.ts:148-151`).
- So a customer with volume data can never reinstall or restore without destroying the volume.
- **Fix:** support moving a volume between the customer's own servers on the same node, or correct the message.

**11. Reinstall keeps the old root password.**
- `index.ts:757` reuses the stored password whenever the server already has a VM ID, which is always true on reinstall.
- **Fix:** generate a new password on REINSTALL.

**12. Firewall script is fragile.**
- No `set -e`, so the exit code is whatever the last line returned; a partial apply is reported as success.
- It assumes `iptables` exists in the guest, but cloud-init only installs qemu-guest-agent. It has only been used on Ubuntu 24.04.
- It connects over SSH with the stored root password, so a customer who changes their password or disables password login breaks it.

### Low

13. **Backups wording:**
    - `page.tsx:743` calls backup storage "separate, redundant". Customer archives actually live on the `tank` pool, which is a single disk (`sda`). The platform's nightly off-site copy is separate from what customers can restore.
    - `page.tsx:759` says "restores are handled by support", yet self-service restore exists.
    - Automatic backups are off by default; only 7 of 37 servers have them on.
14. **Reverse DNS (rDNS) is admin-only** (`lib/actions-ovh.ts:30`). `setDedicatedReverse` quietly does nothing if the provider isn't configured (`lib/dedicated-ip.ts:421-431`), and the PTR record isn't reset when an IP goes back to the pool.
15. **The crash-recovery sweep restarts servers customers shut down themselves.** It restarts any VM marked RUNNING in the DB that is found powered off, including after an in-guest `poweroff`, within about 5 minutes (`worker/vm-recovery.ts:35,62-69`).
16. **A server being deleted shows "Building your server"**, because DELETING counts as transitional (`page.tsx:340` / `Provisioning.tsx:242`).
17. **Port forwards:**
    - `addPortForward` doesn't reject a duplicate guest port, although a comment in `NetworkingControls.tsx:14-19` says it does.
    - The "Allow HTTP (80)" preset actually maps a random public port between 20000 and 29999.
    - A NAT VPS can't serve on ports 80/443 at all.
18. **Overview "Create backup" button** is only a link to the Backups tab (`VpsOverviewPanel.tsx:442`).
19. **Failed-resize refund:** if a resize fails after the plan was already switched, the customer is refunded without the plan being switched back (`index.ts:1846` vs `2432-2439`).
20. **SSH keys** are only injected at provision/reinstall; deleting a key from the account doesn't remove it from existing servers. The UI copy is honest about this.
21. **Suspended banner** links to "Open a ticket" instead of the billing page, which is where an unpaid suspension is actually settled.
22. **NxCloud** is switched off (`nxcloud_ordering_enabled=false`, 0 instances). If it's enabled later, its backing server is still reachable at `/dashboard/servers/[id]` with full reinstall/delete controls, and `terminateNxcloud` gives no refund and doesn't check for a running job.

---

## Working end to end

- **Power start/stop/reboot:** `serverAction` (`lib/actions.ts:762`) → `powerAction` (`worker/index.ts:1394`). All DONE in the last 30 days.
- **Reinstall, same OS or a new OS:** `reinstallToOs` (`lifecycle.ts:121`) → `reinstall()` (`index.ts:1569`), with a guard for attached volumes. 4 DONE.
- **Resize up with proration:** `resizeServer` → `applyResize` (`lib/resize.ts:158`) → `resize()` (`index.ts:1790`), refund on failure (`index.ts:2414`). Only exercised once on a VPS (July).
- **Disk expand:** `expandServerDisk` → `worker/disk-expand.ts` (grows the filesystem online, refunds if it fails). 5 DONE.
